reasoning: Root cause, the URL-rewrite mechanism and every rejected alternative are dated command output, the RED is #277's own failure moved onto `main`, and D4 now keeps the two empty-profile proofs by comparing them against the harness's own file instead of relaxing them.

simpler.evidence: design.md D1 rejects four cheaper mechanisms, each with the proof it would destroy, verified against the real tests: a stub `pre-commit` (tests/publisher/test_init_remote.py:549 `test_pre_push_hook_is_installed` and :628 `test_foreign_pre_push_is_migrated` would then assert the stub's hook file and `pre-push.legacy` move), `git push --no-verify` in `Runner` (the logged command would stop being the command run, so `_pushes(runner)` would prove nothing about the hook), `core.hooksPath` (init reads it as a blocked clone — the arranged state of test_init_remote.py:605 `test_pre_push_blocked_is_manual` — so the pre-push step tests would stop running), and the real `language: python` hook repository behind the mapping (a pip install per fresh cache; test_quality.py:231 covers it through `try-repo <ROOT>`). D3's probe manifest is not decoration: the fixture repository carries no root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, so with D1's mapping alone pre-commit would fail on a missing hook id `quality` — the manifest is what makes the guarded push succeed at all, and the recorded file is the only assertion that the hook ran rather than being silently skipped (§IV). D4 adds two small harness functions with two call sites each and rejects the one-line alternative (skipping `.gitconfig` in `snapshot`) because it would let an `init` write to the user's global git config pass. Total: two config sections, one fixture file, no production code, no new script.

map.evidence: `.openspec.yaml` sets `skip_specs: true` and proposal — Capabilities declares no modified capability, so there is no delta scenario to map. tasks.md `## Scenario → test map` records `n/a: skip_specs` and names the covering tests: the new `test_init_remote.py::test_sandbox_push_runs_the_local_hook` and the five of #277 (`test_init_config.py::test_update_keeps_consumer_bytes`, the four `test_consumer_session_start_is_not_owned[*]`).

red.evidence: Task 1.1 lands the D2 guard without D1's mapping, so the failure is #277's own: `install(..., "--confirm")` returns 1 on the pre-commit clone and each of the six selected tests fails inside its body at an `assert install(...) == 0`. The same task carries D4's two assertions and requires them green before the RED commit, so the RED set is exactly the intended tests and nothing else in the suite is red for a foreign reason — the gap of the previous round, since `check_red` judges only the node ids it is given (check_red.py:258-262) and would not have seen `test_init.py`. Task 1.2 names the expected failure mode, so a failure for another reason is visible; the unparametrized `test_consumer_session_start_is_not_owned` id expands to its four cases in the runner's own report, and `skipped` counts as not-green (check_red.py:67), so a machine without `pre-commit` could not be mistaken for RED.

platform.evidence: Every behaviour the design rests on is command output, dated 2026-09-30 against pre-commit 4.6.0 (the pinned dev dependency), recorded in proposal — Why: (a) with `url.file:///no-network/.insteadOf = https://` alone, `pre-commit run quality --hook-stage pre-push` exits 3 with `Please make sure you have the correct access rights and the repository exists`; (b) with the longer `url.<local repo>.insteadOf = https://github.com/ekolvah/agent-process-distribution` added, exit 0, `[INFO] Initializing environment for https://github.com/ekolvah/agent-process-distribution.`, `quality ... Passed`, and the probe wrote its file — so both git's longest-prefix rule and the fact that pre-commit's clone reads the sandbox's `$HOME/.gitconfig` are observed, not asserted. The reproduction of the defect itself is #277's CI failure plus the local `git checkout v3.2.3 -> error: pathspec 'v3.2.3' did not match` on the release branch. D3 now double-quotes the interpreter path in the `entry`, so pre-commit's shlex split keeps a path with a space one word. Implementer note, not a finding: `Path.write_text` translates `\n` to `\r\n` on Windows, which would make the file's bytes differ from `gitconfig(sb).encode()` — write the bytes (or `newline=""`) so D4's baseline is exact; task 1.1's "verify that both pass" catches it on the spot.

replaced.evidence: Replaced input: how a sandbox git command resolves `https://` — the network becomes the fixture's local `process.git` (D1) or a non-existent path (D2). Dropped guard, recorded: since #276 a sandbox push incidentally proved the published repository at `v{CURRENT}` is fetchable; design — Goals states the new contract (`whatever tags the real repository has`) and names the replacement coverage — `test_quality.py::test_hook_repository_runs_at_pre_push` for the real `language: python` hook and `test_init_config.py:171 test_pre_commit_block_references_the_hook` for the rendered `repo`/`rev` strings; the residual gap (a published tag exists) is the defect itself and belongs to the release, not to the suite. The second replaced input, raised as last round's finding, is now answered by D4: `consumer_repo`'s new `$HOME/.gitconfig` would have broken `tests/publisher/test_init.py:133` `snapshot(sandbox.home) == {}` and `:289` `snapshot(sandbox.root, sandbox.home) == {}` (init_harness.snapshot walks every file and skips only `.git`). One renderer `gitconfig(sb)` is both what `consumer_repo` writes and what `home_baseline(sb)` expects, so the proof is preserved rather than relaxed — any other `init` write under `home`, and any drift of that file's bytes, still fails both tests, and the baseline follows task 2.1's added section automatically. `tests/publisher/test_init.py` is now in proposal — Impact, so task 3.2's diff check holds. Every other snapshot of `home` in the suite is a before/after comparison within one test (test_init.py:65/81/109/118/143/145, test_init_conflicts.py:243/249, test_init_remote.py:295/306/345/352/360), unaffected.

catcher.evidence: Three catchers, all traceable. (1) The D2 guard: any future `https://` git URL a test or an `init` change reaches is rewritten to `file:///no-network/...` and the clone fails at once with the observed error, surfacing as a failing test in task 2.2, in task 3.2's `python .agent-process/scripts/ci_check.py` and in the CI pytest job of the delivery PR — instead of today's pass-only-while-network-and-tag-exist (§IV). (2) D4's `home_baseline`: an `init` write under `home`, including one to the global git config, fails the two `test_init.py` assertions in the same runs. (3) A machine without `pre-commit` on PATH: `init` plans no `pre-push` step (test_init_remote.py:605 documents that state), the record is absent and `test_sandbox_push_runs_the_local_hook` fails naming `home/pre-push-ran`; `pre-commit` is pinned in `.agent-process/requirements-dev.txt`, which the quality `setup` installs. A silent regression of the mapping (a pre-commit change, a moved cache) lands back on catcher 1, so the failure mode of the fix is red, never green-by-network.

length.evidence: The plan adds and edits no rule and no spec sentence: `skip_specs: true`, proposal — Capabilities is empty, and Impact lists four test-harness files and nothing else. Words of added rule text: 0; words its tests assert: 0.

bespoke.evidence: No script, gate or check is added — the change is two rendered git-config sections, two harness functions and one fixture file. The fixture file carries its decision (D3): the problem it closes (the fixture repository has no root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, so the locally resolved `quality` hook would not exist) and the standard for its job rejected with an observed reason (the repository's real `language: python` manifest needs a `pip install` per fresh cache; D1's last bullet, covered by test_quality.py:231). D4 likewise names its rejected standard. This respects the repository's rule that new deterministic checks arrive only after an observed problem.
